I'm encountering issues with the search function. Let me analyze the statements based on my knowledge of chemistry:

A. "A vapor pressure - in some cases very small - develops above every liquid"
This statement is correct. Every liquid has molecules that can escape into the gas phase, creating a vapor pressure. Even liquids with strong intermolecular forces will have some molecules with enough energy to escape into the vapor phase, though this pressure may be extremely small for some substances.

B. "Liquids with a high vapor pressure evaporate rapidly in an open vessel"
This statement is correct. Vapor pressure is a measure of a liquid's tendency to evaporate. Liquids with high vapor pressures (like acetone or gasoline) have weaker intermolecular forces, allowing molecules to escape more easily from the liquid phase, resulting in faster evaporation.

C. "Vapor pressures are always below or at 1 bar"
This statement is incorrect. While many common liquids at room temperature have vapor pressures below 1 bar, this is not a universal rule. Vapor pressure increases with temperature, and many substances can have vapor pressures exceeding 1 bar at higher temperatures. For example, water at its critical point (374°C) has a vapor pressure of 221 bar.

D. "When the vapor pressure of a liquid reaches the ambient pressure, it begins to boil"
This statement is correct. Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure. At this point, bubbles of vapor can form throughout the liquid, not just at the surface, which is the definition of boiling.

Based on my analysis, statements A, B, and D are correct.
